title: Explain async/await and the Task Parallel Library in C#

data.text: **Question:** Explain async/await and the Task Parallel Library in C#

async/await is syntactic sugar that simplifies working with Tasks. The Task Parallel Library (TPL) provides the underlying infrastructure for parallel and asynchronous programming using the Task class.

**async/await:**
- Makes asynchronous code look synchronous
- The compiler transforms async methods into state machines
- await yields control without blocking the thread
- Exceptions are captured and rethrown at the await point

**Task Parallel Library (TPL):**
- Provides Task and Task<T> for asynchronous operations
- Task.Run queues work to the ThreadPool
- Parallel.For/ForEach for data parallelism
- Supports cancellation via CancellationToken
- Supports progress reporting via IProgress<T>

Interviewers want to assess:
- Understanding of async method signatures
- Knowledge of Task vs ValueTask
- Awareness of deadlock scenarios
- Proper use of ConfigureAwait

items: Using async void instead of async Task
Forgetting to await tasks (fire and forget)
Blocking on async code with .Result or .Wait()
Not using ConfigureAwait in library code
What is the difference between Task and ValueTask?
How do you handle exceptions in async methods?
What is the purpose of ConfigureAwait(false)?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always handle exceptions in async methods
data.takeaway: Use async/await for I/O-bound operations and Task.Run for CPU-bound work.
